content.text:
I've submitted candidate **#135** (Cu 0.60, Fe 0.14, V 0.26) as the best composition. At 6.5 µA it had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured.

| Index | Cu / Fe / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 24 | 0.11 / 0.14 / 0.75 | 2.55 µA |
| 131 | 0.54 / 0.13 / 0.33 | 3.83 µA |
| 135 | 0.60 / 0.14 / 0.26 | 6.5 µA |

The budget allowed only three merit measurements, so this is a small sample. Photocurrent rose with copper content across the three points. I chose the first two from general knowledge that copper vanadates are good photoanodes, testing one copper-rich and one vanadium-rich composition. The Gaussian-process tool also suggested #135 for the last measurement.

I didn't know whether #135 beats the rest of the library. Compositions with even more copper (Cu around 0.62–0.65, such as #143 or #169) weren't tested and could be higher.

I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so which crystal phases are present is unknown. I also couldn't read the list of known phases: it was too large to return and was saved to a file I had no tool to open.
